description: Retrieval as a tool in an agent loop: the model decides whether, where and how often to search, reformulates queries and checks whether the evidence is sufficient.
A question that needs facts from several passages combined in steps, such as finding a plan and then its refund rule.
Deciding whether retrieved evidence answers the question before generating, and searching again or saying "not found" when it does not.
Sending whole documents or a whole corpus in a large context window instead of retrieving passages.
Degrading model performance as input length grows, even when the window accepts the input; worse for facts in the middle and with little lexical overlap.
The finding that models use information at the start and end of a long context better than information in the middle.
Research approaches where the model decides when to retrieve and critiques passages (Self-RAG) or grades retrieval and falls back to other sources (CRAG).

term: Routing between RAG and long context
description: Answering with retrieval first and escalating to long context when the model judges the passages insufficient, trading cost for quality only when needed.
